name: Ad Hoc
summary: Reactive, unstructured detection with minimal process or visibility. Default telemetry and vendor detection content are on; what happens next depends on who is on shift.

gates.why: Some record exists of what telemetry is collected.

name: Defined
summary: Documented processes, basic tooling, limited threat-intelligence use. The first attack trees exist for the top crown-jewel objectives and deployed detections are mapped to ATT&CK.

gates.why: Attack trees drawn for at least the top crown-jewel objectives.

name: Managed
summary: Threat intelligence informs operations; SIEM/EDR (or cloud-native equivalents) well integrated. Attack trees and threat models exist for all crown-jewel objectives and every in-scope detection traces to one.

gates.why: Intelligence reliably produces detection work with tracked disposition.
Attack trees cover the prioritised adversary objectives, ATT&CK-mapped.
Detections trace back to the model node that justified them.
Detection content is version-controlled and peer-reviewed.

name: Predictive
summary: Proactive hunting and behavioural analytics proportionate to the behaviour being detected — the model mandates outcomes, never a specific technology. Detection claims are proven by emulation, and deception is placed at attack-tree choke points.

gates.why: Technique-level testing runs on a cadence with recorded outcomes.
Prioritised actors are emulated as full chains, not isolated techniques.
Deception is deployed at modelled choke points.

name: Optimized
summary: Fully integrated and continuously improved: threat change automatically produces telemetry, detection and validation change, with measured cycle time. Autonomy where it is safe, evidence everywhere.

gates.why: Findings close through a measured, re-tested loop.
Improvement is a managed cadence with demonstrated progression.
